Convert a Word or PowerPoint file to Markdown using Pandoc

convert_markdown.Rd

Converts a Microsoft Word (.docx) or PowerPoint (.pptx) file to Markdown using Pandoc. Media (e.g., embedded images) and citations can be extracted if requested. The function returns the path to the generated Markdown file and, optionally, the directory where media was saved

Usage

convert_markdown(
  input_file,
  markdown_file = "markdown_output.md",
  media_base_dir = ".",
  pandoc_args = NULL,
  pandoc_version = "default",
  verbose = FALSE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

input_file

Path to the input file to convert. Must be a .docx or .pptx file.

markdown_file

Path to the output Markdown file. The file will be overwritten if it already exists. Defaults to "markdown_output.md".

media_base_dir

Path to the base directory where extracted media should be saved. Pandoc will create a subfolder named media/ inside this directory (e.g., path/to/base/media/) and extract all embedded media files here. The directory is only created if media is present in the input file.

  • Set to NULL to disable media extraction entirely.

  • Set to "." (the default) to extract media into the current working directory ./media/.

pandoc_args

Additional command-line arguments passed to Pandoc, for example "--wrap=none" or "--to=markdown+pipe_tables+grid_tables". Provide as a single string or character vector. Non-default markdown targets can change citation escaping, so clean_markdown(clean_citations = TRUE) may be useful downstream. Defaults to NULL.

pandoc_version

Pandoc version to use. Passed directly to pandoc::pandoc_run(). Defaults to "default". If the default Pandoc is missing or older than 3.8.3, a Pandoc bundled with RStudio/Positron (RSTUDIO_PANDOC) or Quarto that meets 3.8.3 is used instead. "latest" can select a Pandoc that doesn't match the bundled one, so it is not the default.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints informative messages about the Pandoc command being executed and the location of extracted media (if any). Defaults to FALSE.

overwrite

Logical; if FALSE, stop rather than write over an existing markdown_file. Defaults to TRUE. Use timestamped_path() to keep earlier versions.

Value

Invisibly returns a named list with:

  • markdown_file – the path to the created Markdown file

  • media_dir – the path to the created media/ directory, or NULL if media extraction was disabled or no media was present

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  convert_markdown("report.docx", pandoc_version = "latest")
  convert_markdown("slides.pptx", media_base_dir = "slides_output")
} # }
